items.confound_note: All four plots sit in the same backyard in the same summer, so they share one weather history. Rainfall roughly double the prior year is a single alternative cause that covers every case at once, and because each plot is compared against itself a year earlier rather than against an untreated plot in the same year, nothing in the evidence separates the fertilizer from the rain.
items.notes: SEED. Cases are IDENTICAL to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. That closer is the shared confound. It only works because the cases are coherent: four plots in one backyard in one summer share a weather history, so one weather fact explains all four.

items.passage:
A gardener's notebook records four plots that were given the same fertilizer.
One: a tomato in the Ellis backyard, fed 3 August, stood 11 cm taller by 20 June than the previous summer; logged by Reyes.
Two: a fern in the Marsh Lane flat, fed 8 January, stood 9 cm taller by 26 February than the previous winter; logged by Okonjo.
Three: an oak in the Aldergate orchard, fed 2 May, stood 13 cm taller by 19 April than the previous spring; logged by Halvard.
Four: a cactus in the Vinter greenhouse, fed 7 October, stood 8 cm taller by 24 November than the previous autumn; logged by Bittner.
Rainfall and mean temperature matched the previous year at every plot, the soil mix was unchanged, and nothing else was altered.
items.confound_note: In cases one and three the height was recorded before the fertilizer was applied: 20 June precedes 3 August, and 19 April precedes 2 May. Half the evidence therefore describes growth that had already happened when the treatment was given, so it cannot be evidence for the treatment. The two remaining cases are not enough on their own.
items.notes: SEED. The closing sentence is IDENTICAL to both TRUE items - the flaw lives entirely in the dates inside cases one and three, which is invisible to a bag-of-ngrams classifier because the tokens are unchanged. A single shared confound cannot be used here: four plants in four places across four seasons share no weather history.
